external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and may manually initiate a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: A runner that fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be manually used to rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand; that path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: A controller that stores which image SHA the estate should use and responds to store server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token to call the controller; the token is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store back office that runs the till software container and polls for the current release.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 stores. Store servers do not get pushed to.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: The till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: A self-hosted git server on the corporate network holding developers' branches and the merged source.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: A registry in the build environment holding container images tagged with commit SHAs and allowing store servers to pull images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server after a merge to main starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry during dependency resolution.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: dependencies downloaded according to the lockfile

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: make release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: Authentication uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: image SHA and current release request

data_flows.name: ask release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs from the release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it. The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually kicks off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

assumptions.assumption: The developer is assigned to the corporate network boundary because the developer accesses the corporate build pipeline and git server.
assumptions.basis: The text places the git server and deploy controller on the corporate network and says developers push to the git server and can log in to the build runner; it does not state a separate developer network.

assumptions.assumption: The git server's source code is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The git server holds developer branches and source code, which is commercially sensitive system material.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry's container images are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The image registry holds finished container images produced from the organization's source code.
